ops.entry: WHEN running check-plan-routes.py DO pass your own plan.yaml FILE: with no argument it reports every live plan, so other features' DEVIATION lines read as yours, and handed a directory it raises IsADirectoryError and exits 1, which reads as a gate failure rather than a bad argument.
ops.why: Merges G-10 into G-05 (same script, same argument rule) to free a Gotchas slot; no longer than the longer input.

ops.entry: WHEN quoting a decisions_affected clause that wraps across a DECISIONS.md line break DO write it as a double-quoted scalar with a literal \n at the break: plan-merge check requires the clause as an exact substring of the decision's section, newlines included, so a space-joined wrap fails as not verbatim.
ops.why: Own log bullet 1; confirmed at control plane plan_merge/check.py _rows_faults (str(clause) not in section). Repository-specific gate behaviour.

originals.original: WHEN running check-plan-routes.py DO pass your own plan's path. With no argument it reports over every live plan, so other features' DEVIATION lines land in your output and read as yours; only the summary line is global.
WHEN running check-plan-routes.py DO pass a plan.yaml FILE: handed the feature directory it raises IsADirectoryError and exits 1, which reads as a gate failure rather than as a bad argument.

ops.entry: WHEN a plan removes a branch that accepts a class of inputs DO enumerate what its predicate actually accepted, including the vacuous instance and data-carrying instances, not only the minimal example, and require a case-level test witness per signed behaviour delta before signature; otherwise deltas surface only by validation probes.
ops.why: Own log bullets 2-3 and both rulings' Gap: the empty instance was caught at intake, the row-carrying foreign-version instance escaped to validate untested. Displaces P-11, which duplicates the preloaded harness-brief red flag (an SC quantifying over more than the work can touch).

ops.entry: WHEN a predicate or criterion names raw input, bytes or exact output DO treat decoded, parsed, trimmed or newline-normalized forms as a different clause: specify which form is contractual, require a case where normalization changes the outcome, and grade a normalized comparison partial, never adequate by argument.
ops.why: My goal-check called a json.loads comparison 'adequate' for a bytes clause; the c1 ruling found a text-mode read let a CRLF mutant pass, costing an escalation. Sharpens G-06 to cover grading as well as specifying; drops its narrow passthrough sub-clause; same length.

originals.original: WHEN a criterion quantifies over a scope DO check, before dispatch, that the tasks tracing to it carry file lists covering that scope. A task naming one file cannot satisfy a clause over every document, so the criterion fails at goal-check for a planning reason no retry can fix.

WHEN a path or input predicate is contractual DO specify whether it classifies raw or normalized input and require cases where normalization changes category. Preserve the original-entry passthrough rule separately; trimming or unquoting before classification can invalidate an otherwise matching predicate.
